title.zh: 卷四百八十一 列傳第二百四十 世家四 南漢劉氏劉鋹(龔澄樞 李托 薛崇譽 潘崇徹)
title.en: Volume 481 Biographies 240: Hereditary Houses 4 - Southern Han and Liu clans Liu Chang (Gong Chengshu, Li Tuo, Xue Chongyu, Pan Chongche)
title.raw: 卷四百八十一 列傳第二百四十 世家四 南漢劉氏劉鋹(龔澄樞 李托 薛崇譽 潘崇徹) Volume 481 Biographies 240: Hereditary Houses 4 - Southern Han and Liu clans Liu Chang (Gong Chengshu, Li Tuo, Xue Chongyu, Pan Chongche)

sentences.zh: 世家四○南漢劉氏

translations.literal: Hereditary Houses 4 ○ The Liu Clan of Southern Han
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary Houses 4: The Liu Clan of Southern Han

sentences.zh: 南漢劉鋹，其先蔡州上蔡人，高祖安仁，仕唐為潮州刺史，因家嶺表。

translations.literal: Liu Chang of Southern Han — his ancestors were men of Shangcai in Cizhou; his great-grandfather Anren served the Tang as prefect of Chaozhou and thereby made his home in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang of Southern Han traced his line to Shangcai in Cizhou. His great-grandfather Anren had served the Tang as prefect of Chaozhou and settled his family in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 安仁生謙，為廣州牙校，累遷封州刺史、賀水鎮遏使。

translations.literal: Anren begot Qian, who served as a military aide at Guangzhou and was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Feng and commissioner for suppressing unrest on the He River.
translations.idiomatic: Anren's son Qian served as a military aide at Guangzhou and rose in time to prefect of Feng and commissioner for suppressing unrest on the He River.

sentences.zh: 謙生隱，謙卒，隱代領其任。

translations.literal: Qian begot Yin; when Qian died, Yin took over his duties in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's son Yin succeeded him when Qian died and assumed his post.

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗以薛王知柔鎮南海，辟為行軍司馬，委以兵柄。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong of Tang appointed Prince of Xue Zhi Rou to govern the Southern Sea and recruited [Yin] as campaigning marshal of the army, entrusting him with military authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong of Tang sent Prince of Xue Zhi Rou to govern the Southern Sea, he recruited Yin as campaigning marshal and entrusted him with military power.

sentences.zh: 及宰相徐彥若代知柔，以為節度副使。

translations.literal: When the chief minister Xu Yanruo replaced Zhi Rou, [Yin] was made deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Minister Xu Yanruo replaced Zhi Rou, Yin was appointed deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時唐室已季，彥若威令不振，事皆決於隱。

translations.literal: By then the Tang house was in its last days; Yanruo's authority did not hold sway, and all affairs were decided by Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang dynasty was already in decline; Yanruo's orders carried no weight, and Yin decided everything.

sentences.zh: 彥若卒，遺表薦隱自代，昭宗不從，以崔遠代之。

translations.literal: When Yanruo died he left a memorial recommending Yin to succeed him; Zhaozong did not agree and sent Cui Yuan to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: On Yanruo's death he memorialized the throne urging that Yin succeed him, but Zhaozong refused and appointed Cui Yuan in his place.

sentences.zh: 遠至江陵，遷延不進，乃以隱為留後，未幾，授以節旄。

translations.literal: Yuan reached Jiangling but delayed and would not advance; Yin was then made acting commissioner, and before long was granted the commissioner's insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan reached Jiangling but lingered without advancing, so Yin was made acting commissioner; shortly afterward he received the commissioner's insignia.

sentences.zh: 梁開平初，兼靜海軍節度使，封南海王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiping under the Liang, [he] also held the post of military commissioner of the Jinghai Army and was enfeoffed as King of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Liang reign era Kaiping, he also became military commissioner of the Jinghai Army and was enfeoffed as King of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 隱卒，弟陟襲位。

translations.literal: When Yin died, his younger brother Yang succeeded to the position.
translations.idiomatic: After Yin died, his younger brother Yang took the throne.

sentences.zh: 貞明三年，僭帝號，國稱大漢，改元乾亨，行郊祀禮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming, [he] presumptuously assumed an imperial title; the state was called Great Han, the era name was changed to Qianheng, and suburban sacrifices were performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenming (917), he declared himself emperor, named his state Great Han, adopted the era name Qianheng, and performed suburban sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 改名岩，又改龔，終改。

translations.literal: He changed his name to Yan, then again to Gong, and finally to a character not recorded in standard lexicons (here rendered as Yan's final form).
translations.idiomatic: He changed his name to Yan, then to Gong, and finally to a character of his own invention (the text's final form).

sentences.zh: 「」讀為「儼」，字書不載，蓋其妄作也。

translations.literal: That final character was read as "yan" (like the word for majestic bearing); it does not appear in dictionaries — presumably his own arbitrary invention.
translations.idiomatic: The final character was pronounced like "yan," as in the word for majestic bearing; it appears in no dictionary and was plainly his own fabrication.

sentences.zh: 晉天福七年，卒，子玢嗣，為弟晟所殺。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianfu under Jin, [he] died; his son Bin succeeded but was killed by his younger brother Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Tianfu (942). His son Bin succeeded him but was killed by his younger brother Sheng.

sentences.zh: 晟遂自立，性尤酷暴，周顯德五年，卒，事具《五代史》。

translations.literal: Sheng then established himself [on the throne]; his nature was especially cruel and violent. In the fifth year of Xiande under Zhou he died; the full account is in the History of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng then seized power himself. He was exceptionally cruel and violent. He died in the fifth year of Xiande (958); the full account is given in the History of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 鋹即晟長子也，初名繼興，封衛王，襲父位，改今名，改元大寶。

translations.literal: Chang was Sheng's eldest son; he was first named Jixing, enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, succeeded his father, took his present name, and changed the era name to Dabao.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was Sheng's eldest son. Originally named Jixing and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, he succeeded his father, adopted his present name, and proclaimed the era name Dabao.

sentences.zh: 性昏懦，委政宦官龔澄樞及才人盧瓊仙，每詳覽可否，皆瓊仙指之。

translations.literal: His nature was dull and timid; he entrusted government to the eunuch Gong Chengshu and the talented lady Lu Qiongxian, and whenever he examined matters in detail for approval or rejection, it was Qiongxian who pointed the way.
translations.idiomatic: Dull and timid by nature, he handed affairs of state to the eunuch Gong Chengshu and the talented consort Lu Qiongxian; on every matter he weighed, it was Qiongxian who guided his decision.

sentences.zh: 鋹日與宮人、波斯女等遊戲。

translations.literal: Chang spent his days in diversions with palace women, Persian women, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Chang passed his days in amusements with palace women and Persian girls.

sentences.zh: 內官陳延壽引女巫樊胡入宮，言玉皇遣樊胡命鋹為太子皇帝，乃於宮中施帷幄，羅列珍玩，設玉皇坐。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Chen Yanshou introduced the witch Fan Hu into the palace, saying the Jade Emperor had sent Fan Hu to command that Chang be crown emperor; then within the palace they hung curtains, arrayed rare treasures, and set up a seat for the Jade Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Chen Yanshou brought the witch Fan Hu into the palace, claiming the Jade Emperor had sent her to name Chang crown emperor. Curtains were hung, rare treasures displayed, and a throne for the Jade Emperor installed.

sentences.zh: 樊胡遠遊冠、紫衣、紫霞裙，坐宣禍福，令鋹再拜聽命；

translations.literal: Fan Hu wore a traveling cap, purple robe, and purple cloud skirt, sat proclaiming fortune and misfortune, and ordered Chang to bow again and listen to commands;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Hu wore a traveling cap, purple robe, and purple cloud skirt, sat pronouncing fortune and disaster, and made Chang bow repeatedly to receive her commands;

sentences.zh: 嘗雲瓊仙、澄樞、延壽皆玉皇遣輔太子皇帝，有過不得治。

translations.literal: She once said that Qiongxian, Chengshu, and Yanshou had all been sent by the Jade Emperor to assist the crown emperor, and that they might not be punished for faults.
translations.idiomatic: She once declared that Qiongxian, Chengshu, and Yanshou had all been sent by the Jade Emperor to assist the crown emperor and could not be punished for any offense.

sentences.zh: 又有梁山師、馬媼、何擬之徒出入宮掖。

translations.literal: There were also Liangshan Shi, Nurse Ma, He Ni, and others of that sort who came and went within the inner palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Others such as Liangshan Shi, Nurse Ma, and He Ni also moved freely through the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 宮中婦人皆具冠帶，領外事。

translations.literal: All women of the palace wore caps and belts and took charge of external affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Every woman in the palace wore official cap and belt and handled affairs outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 初，雖寵任中官，其數裁三百餘，位不過掖庭諸局令丞。

translations.literal: At first, though [the earlier ruler] favored eunuchs, their number was limited to somewhat over three hundred and their ranks did not exceed the various bureau directors and assistants of the palace women.
translations.idiomatic: At first, even though the court favored eunuchs, their number was barely three hundred, and none rose above the rank of director or assistant in the palace women's bureaus.

sentences.zh: 至晟時千餘人，稍增內常侍、諸謁者之稱。

translations.literal: Under Sheng there were more than a thousand, and titles such as inner regular attendant and various ushers were gradually added.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sheng they exceeded a thousand, and titles such as inner regular attendant and palace usher were gradually introduced.

sentences.zh: 至鋹漸至七千餘，有為三師、三公，但其上加「內」字，諸使名不翅二百，女官亦有師傅、令仆之號。

translations.literal: Under Chang they gradually reached more than seven thousand; some held the ranks of the Three Preceptors and Three Dukes, but with the prefix "inner" added to the title; there were no fewer than two hundred envoy designations, and female officials too had masters, tutors, and chancellor-style titles.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chang the number rose to more than seven thousand. Some held the ranks of the Three Preceptors and Three Dukes with the word "inner" prefixed; envoy titles alone numbered at least two hundred, and female officials bore titles such as master, tutor, director, and vice-director.

sentences.zh: 目百官為「門外人」，群臣小過及士人、釋、道有才略可備問者，皆下蠶室，令得出入宮闈。

translations.literal: He called the hundred officials "people outside the gates"; any minister's minor fault, or any scholar, Buddhist, or Daoist with talent worth consulting, was sent to the silkworm chamber so they could come and go within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He called the civil officials "outsiders at the gate." Ministers guilty of minor faults, and any scholar, monk, or priest of talent fit for consultation, were castrated and allowed to move in and out of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 作燒煮剝剔、刀山劍樹之刑，或令罪人鬥虎抵象。

translations.literal: He devised punishments of burning, boiling, flaying, knife mountains, and sword trees, or had culprits fight tigers and elephants.
translations.idiomatic: He invented tortures of burning, boiling, flaying, knife mountains, and sword trees, or forced criminals to fight tigers and elephants.

sentences.zh: 又賦斂煩重，邕民入城者人輸一錢，瓊州米斗稅四五錢。

translations.literal: Levies were also heavy and vexatious: those of Yong entering the city paid one cash each, and on Qiongzhou rice was taxed at four or five cash per dou.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were oppressive as well: every resident of Yong who entered the capital paid one cash, and in Qiongzhou each dou of rice was taxed four or five cash.

sentences.zh: 置媚川都，定其課，令入海五百尺采珠。

translations.literal: He established the Meichuan Directorate, fixed its levy, and ordered men to dive five hundred feet into the sea to gather pearls.
translations.idiomatic: He set up the Meichuan Directorate, fixed its quota, and ordered divers five hundred feet down into the sea to collect pearls.

sentences.zh: 所居宮殿以珠、玳瑁飾之。

translations.literal: The palaces where he dwelt were decorated with pearls and tortoise shell.
translations.idiomatic: The palaces he lived in were ornamented with pearls and tortoise shell.

sentences.zh: 陳延壽作諸淫巧，日費數萬金。

translations.literal: Chen Yanshou fashioned all manner of lewd curiosities, costing tens of thousands in gold each day.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yanshou devised every sort of licentious novelty, spending tens of thousands in gold every day.

sentences.zh: 宮城左右離宮數十，鋹遊幸常至月餘或旬日。

translations.literal: Dozens of detached palaces stood to either side of the royal city, and Chang's pleasure excursions often lasted more than a month or ten days at a time.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen detached palaces flanked the capital, and Chang's tours of pleasure often lasted a month or more, sometimes ten days at a stretch.

sentences.zh: 以豪民為課戶，供宴犒之費。

translations.literal: Wealthy households were made tax households to supply the cost of feasts and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families were designated tax households to fund banquets and rewards.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，太祖命師克郴州，獲其內品十餘人。

translations.literal: In the Qiande era, Emperor Taizu ordered his armies to take Chen prefecture and captured more than ten of [Southern Han's] inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiande, Emperor Taizu ordered his forces to capture Chen prefecture and took more than ten of Southern Han's palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 有餘延業者，人質麼麽，太祖問曰：「爾在嶺南為何官？

translations.literal: Among them was one Yu Yanye, of wretched petty quality; the Emperor asked, "What office did you hold in Lingnan?
translations.idiomatic: One was Yu Yanye, a man of wretchedly slight build. The Emperor asked, "What post did you hold in Lingnan?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「為扈駕弓箭手官。

translations.literal: " He replied, "I was officer of the bowmen who escort the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "I was officer of the bowmen who escort the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 」命授之弓矢，延業極力控弦不開。

translations.literal: " He was ordered given bow and arrows; Yanye strained with all his might at the string but could not draw it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor had bow and arrows handed to him; Yanye pulled with all his strength but could not draw the string.

sentences.zh: 太祖因笑問鋹為治之跡，延業備言其奢酷，太祖驚駭曰：「吾當救此一方之民。」

translations.literal: The Emperor therefore laughed and asked about the traces of Chang's governance; Yanye fully described his extravagance and cruelty, and the Emperor said in alarm, "I must rescue the people of this region."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed and asked how Chang governed. Yanye described his extravagance and cruelty in full, and the Emperor said in alarm, "I must save the people of that land."

sentences.zh: 先是，晟因湖南馬氏之亂，襲取桂、郴、賀等州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sheng had taken advantage of the turmoil of the Ma clan in Hunan to seize Gui, Chen, He, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, taking advantage of the Ma clan's disorder in Hunan, Sheng had seized Gui, Chen, He, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 開寶初，鋹又舉兵侵道州，刺史王繼勳上言。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaibao, Chang again raised troops to invade Dao prefecture; the prefect Wang Jixun memorialized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaibao, Chang again marched against Dao prefecture, and Prefect Wang Jixun submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 鋹為政昏暴，民被其毒，請討之。

translations.literal: [The memorial said that] Chang's government was benighted and violent and the people suffered under him, and requested a campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's rule was benighted and brutal, the people groaned under him, and [Wang] asked that he be attacked.

sentences.zh: 太祖難其事，令江南李煜遣使以書諭鋹使稱臣，歸湖南舊地。

translations.literal: Taizu found the undertaking difficult and ordered Li Yu of Jiangnan to send envoys with a letter urging Chang to declare himself a subject and restore the old Hunan territories.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu hesitated over the campaign and ordered Li Yu of Jiangnan to send envoys with a letter urging Chang to submit as a vassal and return the former Hunan lands.

sentences.zh: 鋹不從。

translations.literal: Chang would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Chang refused.

sentences.zh: 煜又遣其給事中龔慎儀遺書曰：

translations.literal: Yu again sent his attendant in the Secretariat Gong Shenyi with a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yu then sent his Secretariat attendant Gong Shenyi with a letter that read:

sentences.zh: 煜與足下叨累世之睦，繼祖考之盟，情若弟兄，義敦交契，憂戚之患，曷嘗不同。

translations.literal: Yu and Your Excellency enjoy the goodwill of many generations and inherit the covenant of our forefathers; in feeling we are like brothers, in righteousness our bond is deep — when have we not shared each other's sorrows and cares?
translations.idiomatic: You and I enjoy the friendship of many generations and inherit the pact our fathers made. In feeling we are brothers; in duty our bond runs deep. Sorrow and trouble — when have we not borne them together?

sentences.zh: 每思會麵而論此懷，抵掌而談此事，交議其所短，各陳其所長；

translations.literal: I often think of meeting face to face to speak this mind, clapping hands together to discuss this matter, each laying bare the other's faults and each setting forth his own strengths;
translations.idiomatic: I often wish we could meet face to face and speak frankly, debate with open hands, each exposing the other's faults and each stating his own strengths;

sentences.zh: 使中心釋然，利害不惑，而相去萬里，斯願莫伸。

translations.literal: so that the heart might be at ease and gain and loss no longer confuse us — yet we are ten thousand li apart, and this wish cannot be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: until our hearts were clear and profit and loss no longer clouded our judgment — but ten thousand li separate us, and that wish cannot be granted.

sentences.zh: 凡於事機不得款會，屢達誠素，冀明此心；

translations.literal: Whenever affairs of the moment could not be discussed in full sincerity, I have repeatedly expressed my honest feeling, hoping to make this heart clear;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever urgent matters could not be discussed in person, I have written again and again in plain sincerity, hoping you would see my true intent;

sentences.zh: 而足下視之，謂書檄一時之儀，近國梗概之事，外貌而待之，泛濫而觀之，使忠告確論如水投石，若此則又何必事虛詞而勞往復哉？

translations.literal: yet Your Excellency has regarded them as mere formal documents of the moment, summary matters of a neighboring state, treating them outwardly and viewing them superficially, so that earnest counsel and solid argument are like water cast on stone — if so, why trouble with empty words and weary exchanges?
translations.idiomatic: yet you have treated them as mere diplomatic formalities, brief notes about a neighbor's affairs — received with outward courtesy and read with indifference, so that honest counsel lands like water on stone. If that is so, why waste words and weary messengers with empty correspondence?

sentences.zh: 殊非宿心之所望也。

translations.literal: This is far from what my long-standing heart has hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: That is far from what I have long hoped for between us.

sentences.zh: 今則復遣人使罄申鄙懷，又慮行人失辭，不盡深素，是以再寄翰墨，重布腹心，以代會麵之談與抵掌之議也。

translations.literal: Now I again send an envoy to express fully my humble mind; yet I fear the traveler may miss his words and not convey the full depth of sincerity, and therefore send this writing once more, laying out again my inmost heart, in place of face-to-face talk and hand-clapping debate.
translations.idiomatic: I now send another envoy to state my thoughts fully, yet I fear he may miss his words and fail to convey my deepest sincerity. I therefore write again and lay bare my heart once more, in place of meeting in person and debating hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 足下誠聽其言如交友諫爭之言，視其心如親戚急難之心，然後三復其言，三思其心，則忠乎不忠，斯可見矣，從乎不從，斯可決矣。

translations.literal: If Your Excellency will truly hear these words as the remonstrance of a friend, and view this heart as the heart of kin in urgent distress, then read them thrice and ponder the mind thrice — whether loyalty or disloyalty will then be plain, and whether to follow or not will then be decided.
translations.idiomatic: Hear these words as a friend's frank counsel; read this heart as a kinsman's cry in desperate need. Read them three times and weigh the intent three times — then whether I speak in loyalty will be clear, and whether you should heed me can be decided.

sentences.zh: 昨以大朝南伐，圖復楚疆，交兵已來，遂成釁隙。

translations.literal: Yesterday the Great Court marched south to recover the Chu territories; since arms were crossed, a breach has formed.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Great Court marched south to recover the Chu lands. Since the armies clashed, a rift has opened between us.

sentences.zh: 詳觀事勢，深切憂懷，冀息大朝之兵，求契親仁之願，引領南望，於今累年。

translations.literal: Observing the situation in detail, I am deeply anxious, hoping to still the armies of the Great Court and fulfill the wish for kinship and benevolence — craning my neck southward, now for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Watching events closely, I have been deeply troubled, longing to see the Great Court's armies stand down and our bond of kinship restored. For years I have strained southward in hope.

sentences.zh: 臨昨使臣入貢大朝，大朝皇帝果以此事宣示曰：「彼若以事大之禮而事我，則何苦而伐之；

translations.literal: When my envoy went recently to pay tribute to the Great Court, the Emperor of the Great Court indeed proclaimed on this matter, saying: "If they will serve me with the rites due a great power, why need I trouble to attack them;
translations.idiomatic: When my envoy lately presented tribute at the Great Court, the Emperor declared on this very matter: "If they will treat me with the ceremony owed a suzerain, why should I trouble to attack them?

sentences.zh: 若欲興戎而爭我，則以必取為度矣。

translations.literal: if they wish to raise arms and contend with me, then I shall take them by force as my measure."
translations.idiomatic: If they wish to take up arms and fight me, I shall regard conquest as inevitable."

sentences.zh: 」見今點閱大眾，仍以上秋為期，令弊邑以書復敘前意，是用奔走人使，遽貢直言。

translations.literal: Now the armies are being mustered, with late autumn still set as the deadline; my humble state was ordered to set forth the earlier intent in writing, and therefore I hasten envoys to offer frank words.
translations.idiomatic: The armies are even now being reviewed, with late autumn still the deadline. My state was told to restate our earlier position in writing, and so I hurry envoys to you with plain speaking.

sentences.zh: 深料大朝之心非有唯利之貪，蓋怒人之不賓而已；

translations.literal: I deeply judge that the heart of the Great Court is not greed for profit alone, but anger that men will not submit as guests;
translations.idiomatic: I am convinced the Great Court is moved not by greed for gain alone, but by anger that subjects refuse to bow;

sentences.zh: 足下非有不得已之事與不可易之謀，殆一時之忿而已。

translations.literal: Your Excellency has no matter of absolute necessity and no plan that cannot be changed — it is likely no more than a moment's wrath.
translations.idiomatic: you have no unavoidable cause and no unalterable design — this is surely no more than a passing fit of anger.

sentences.zh: 觀夫古之用武者，不顧小大強弱之殊而必戰者有四；

translations.literal: Observing those who used arms in antiquity, there are four cases in which they fought regardless of differences of size and strength;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, rulers went to war regardless of relative strength in only four circumstances:

sentences.zh: 父母宗廟之仇，此必戰也；

translations.literal: feud over parents and ancestral temples — in this case one must fight;
translations.idiomatic: vengeance for parents and ancestral temples — war was inevitable;

sentences.zh: 彼此烏合，民無定心，存亡之機以戰為命，此必戰也；

translations.literal: both sides a rabble, the people without settled hearts, survival or ruin hanging on battle — in this case one must fight;
translations.idiomatic: when both sides were mere rabbles, the people unsettled, and survival itself depended on fighting — war was inevitable;

sentences.zh: 敵人有進，必不舍我，求和不得，退守無路，戰亦亡，不戰亦亡，奮不顧命，此必戰也；

translations.literal: the enemy advances and will not let us go, peace cannot be sought, retreat offers no road — to fight is to perish, not to fight is to perish, and one stakes life recklessly — in this case one must fight;
translations.idiomatic: when the enemy pressed on relentlessly, peace was impossible, and retreat offered no escape — to fight was death, not to fight was death, and men threw away their lives — war was inevitable;

sentences.zh: 彼有天亡之兆，我懷進取之機，此必戰也。

translations.literal: the other side shows signs of Heaven's withdrawal, and we hold an opportunity for advance — in this case one must fight.
translations.idiomatic: when Heaven showed the foe was doomed and we held our chance to advance — war was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 今足下與大朝非有父母宗廟之仇也，非同烏合存亡之際也，既殊進退不舍、奮不顧命也，又異乘機進取之時也。

translations.literal: Now Your Excellency and the Great Court have no feud over parents and ancestral temples, are not in the moment of rabble survival, are unlike the case of advance without relent and life staked recklessly, and differ from the time of seizing opportunity to advance.
translations.idiomatic: You and the Great Court bear no feud of parents and temples; you are not two rabble armies fighting for bare survival; you are not cornered with no retreat; nor are you seizing Heaven's moment to strike.

sentences.zh: 無故而坐受天下之兵，將決一旦之命，既大朝許以通好，又拒而不從，有國家、利社稷者當若是乎？

translations.literal: Without cause to sit and receive the armies of the empire, staking the fate of a single morning — when the Great Court has offered peace and you refuse and will not follow — should one who has a state and seeks the altars' good act thus?
translations.idiomatic: Without cause you would invite the armies of the empire and stake your realm on a single throw. The Great Court has offered peace, yet you refuse. Is that how a ruler who loves his state and altars should act?

sentences.zh: 夫稱帝稱王，角立傑出，今古之常事也；

translations.literal: To style oneself emperor or king and stand rival among heroes is a constant affair of past and present;
translations.idiomatic: To call oneself emperor or king and stand as a rival power is as old as history itself;

sentences.zh: 割地以通好，玉帛以事人，亦古今之常事也。

translations.literal: to cede territory to secure peace and offer jade and silk to serve another is also a constant affair of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: and to cede land for peace and send tribute in jade and silk is equally an age-old practice.

sentences.zh: 盈虛消息、取與翕張，屈伸萬端，在我而已，何必膠柱而用壯，輕禍而爭雄哉？

translations.literal: Fullness and emptiness, waxing and waning, taking and giving, closing and opening — bending and stretching have ten thousand forms, and depend on oneself alone; why must one cling to the peg and use force, treat disaster lightly and contend for supremacy?
translations.idiomatic: Fortune rises and falls; giving and taking, advance and retreat — all lie in your own hands. Why cling stubbornly to force, treat disaster lightly, and fight for supremacy?

sentences.zh: 且足下以英明之姿，撫百越之眾，北距五嶺，南負重溟，藉累世之基，有及民之澤，眾數十萬，表裏山川，此足下所以慨然而自負也。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Excellency with an enlightened bearing governs the peoples of the Hundred Yue, with the Five Ridges to the north and the deep sea to the south, relying on foundations of many generations and possessing grace that reaches the people — forces in the hundreds of thousands, mountains and rivers within and without — this is why Your Excellency sighs and takes pride.
translations.idiomatic: You are gifted and enlightened, ruling the peoples of the Hundred Yue, with the Five Ridges to the north and the deep sea behind you, heir to generations of power, blessed with grace that reaches your people, armies in the hundreds of thousands, mountains and rivers as your shield — no wonder you feel proud.

sentences.zh: 然違天不祥，好戰危事，天方相楚，尚未可爭。

translations.literal: Yet to oppose Heaven is inauspicious, and fondness for war is a perilous affair; Heaven is now favoring Chu, and contention is not yet possible.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to defy Heaven is ill-omened, and love of war is perilous. Heaven now favors Chu; the moment to fight has not come.

sentences.zh: 恭以大朝師武臣力，實謂天讚也。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider the military might and ministerial strength of the Great Court — truly I call it Heaven's approval.
translations.idiomatic: I look at the Great Court's armies and ministers and see Heaven's clear approval.

sentences.zh: 登太行而伐上黨，士無難色；

translations.literal: They ascended the Taihang to attack Shangdang, and the soldiers showed no troubled faces;
translations.idiomatic: They climbed the Taihang to strike Shangdang, and the troops did not flinch;

sentences.zh: 絕劍閣而舉庸蜀，役不淹時。

translations.literal: they cut through Jian'ge and raised Yong and Shu, and the campaign did not exceed its season.
translations.idiomatic: they crossed Jian'ge and subdued Yong and Shu before the season turned.

sentences.zh: 是知大朝之力難測也，萬里之境難保也。

translations.literal: From this one knows that the power of the Great Court is hard to measure and a realm of ten thousand li is hard to defend.
translations.idiomatic: This shows how immeasurable the Great Court's strength is, and how hard a realm of ten thousand li is to hold.

sentences.zh: 十戰而九勝，亦一敗可憂；

translations.literal: Nine victories in ten battles — yet one defeat is cause for worry;
translations.idiomatic: Nine victories in ten battles still leave one defeat to dread;

sentences.zh: 六奇而五中，則一失何補！

translations.literal: five hits among six stratagems — then what does one miss repair!
translations.idiomatic: five of six stratagems succeed — yet what good is the one that fails?

sentences.zh: 況人自以我國險，家自以我兵強，蓋揣於此而不揣於彼，經其成而末經其敗也。

translations.literal: Moreover, each man thinks his own state perilous, each household thinks its own troops strong — likely measuring this side and not that, having seen success but not yet seen defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Men trust in their rugged land and strong armies, measuring only their own side, not the enemy's — they have seen victory but not yet defeat.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 國莫險於劍閣，而庸蜀已亡矣；

translations.literal: No state was more perilous than [the land of] Jian'ge, yet Yong and Shu are already lost;
translations.idiomatic: No land was more defensible than Jian'ge, yet Yong and Shu fell;

sentences.zh: 兵莫強於上黨，而太行不守矣。

translations.literal: no troops were stronger than those of Shangdang, yet the Taihang could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: no army was stronger than that of Shangdang, yet the Taihang could not be held.

sentences.zh: 人之情，端坐而思之，意滄海可涉也，及風濤驟興，奔舟失馭，與夫坐思之時蓋有殊矣。

translations.literal: It is human nature: sitting upright in thought, one imagines the blue sea can be crossed — but when wind and waves rise suddenly and the fleeing boat loses its helm, it is quite unlike the time of sitting in thought.
translations.idiomatic: Human nature is thus: sitting at ease, one thinks the ocean can be crossed; but when wind and waves rise and the boat loses its helm, the reality is nothing like the reverie.

sentences.zh: 是以智者慮於未萌，機者重其先見；

translations.literal: Therefore the wise plan before things sprout, and the quick value foresight;
translations.idiomatic: The wise plan before trouble sprouts; the shrewd prize foresight;

sentences.zh: 圖難於其易，居存不忘亡，故曰計禍不及，慮福過之。

translations.literal: they plot difficulty in its ease and dwell in survival without forgetting ruin — hence it is said that reckoning of disaster falls short while pondering of fortune goes too far.
translations.idiomatic: they tackle hardship while it is still easy and live in security without forgetting ruin. Hence the saying: we reckon disaster too little and dream of fortune too much.

sentences.zh: 良以福者人之所樂，心樂之，故其望也過；

translations.literal: Truly because fortune is what men delight in — the heart delights in it, and therefore hope for it goes too far;
translations.idiomatic: Fortune is what men love, and because the heart loves it, hope runs too high;

sentences.zh: 禍者人之所惡，心惡之，故其思也忽。

translations.literal: disaster is what men detest — the heart detests it, and therefore thought of it is slight.
translations.idiomatic: disaster is what men hate, and because the heart hates it, thought runs too low.

sentences.zh: 是以福或修於慊望，禍多出於不期。

translations.literal: Therefore fortune is sometimes built on satisfied hope, while disaster mostly comes from the unlooked-for.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune is often built on satisfied hopes; disaster usually arrives unlooked-for.

sentences.zh: 又或慮有矜功好名之臣，獻尊主強國之議者，必曰：「慎無和也。

translations.literal: Again, one may fear there are ministers who boast of merit and love renown, offering counsel to honor the ruler and strengthen the state, who will surely say: "Be careful — do not make peace.
translations.idiomatic: You may also hear ministers hungry for glory urging you to exalt your throne and strengthen your realm. They will say: "Do not sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 五嶺之險，山高水深，輜重不並行，士卒不成列；

translations.literal: The peril of the Five Ridges — mountains high and waters deep — baggage trains cannot march abreast, soldiers cannot form ranks;
translations.idiomatic: The Five Ridges are impassable — mountains high, waters deep; supply trains cannot march abreast, troops cannot keep formation;

sentences.zh: 高壘清野而絕其運糧，依山阻水而射以強弩，使進無所得，退無所歸。

translations.literal: raise high ramparts and clear the countryside to cut off their grain transport, rely on mountains and block waters to shoot them with strong crossbows, so that advancing they gain nothing and retreating they have nowhere to return."
translations.idiomatic: raise ramparts, strip the countryside, cut their grain lines, hold the mountains and waters, and shoot them with heavy crossbows until advance gains nothing and retreat finds no road home."

sentences.zh: 」此其一也。

translations.literal: " This is the first argument.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first argument.

sentences.zh: 又或曰：「彼所長者，利在平地，今舍其所長，就其所短，雖有百萬之眾，無若我何。

translations.literal: Others will say: "Their strength lies in level ground; now they abandon what they excel at and take up what they lack — though they have a million men, they can do nothing to us.
translations.idiomatic: Others will say: "Their strength is on open ground. If they leave that and fight where we excel, a million men cannot touch us.

sentences.zh: 」此其二也。

translations.literal: " This is the second.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second.

sentences.zh: 其次或曰：「戰而勝，則霸業可成，戰而不勝，則泛巨舟而浮滄海，終不為人下。

translations.literal: Next some will say: "If we fight and win, hegemony can be achieved; if we fight and do not win, we launch great ships and float on the blue sea — we shall never be beneath another.
translations.idiomatic: Still others will say: "Win, and empire is ours; lose, and we sail great ships upon the open sea — we shall never bow to another.

sentences.zh: 」此大約皆說士孟浪之談，謀臣捭闔之策，坐而論之也則易，行之如意也則難。

translations.literal: " These are all roughly the reckless talk of persuaders and the stratagems of plotting ministers — easy to discuss sitting down, hard to carry out as wished.
translations.idiomatic: Such talk is the loose bragging of itinerant persuaders and the schemes of court plotters — easy at the desk, hard in the field.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 今荊湘以南、庸蜀之地，皆是便山水、習險阻之民，不動中國之兵，精卒已逾於十萬矣。

translations.literal: Now south of Jing and Xiang and in the lands of Yong and Shu are all peoples skilled in mountains and waters, accustomed to perilous terrain — without moving the armies of the Central Court, crack troops already exceed a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: South of Jing and Xiang, in Yong and Shu, live peoples at home in mountains and rivers, trained in rugged country. Without even moving the central armies, elite troops already exceed a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 況足下與大朝封疆接畛，水陸同途，殆雞犬之相聞，豈馬牛之不及？

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Excellency and the Great Court share contiguous borders, the same routes by water and land — almost within hearing of each other's chickens and dogs; how could horses and oxen not reach?
translations.idiomatic: Your borders touch the Great Court's on every side; water and land routes are the same. Neighbors can hear each other's dogs bark — how could armies fail to reach you?

sentences.zh: 一旦緣邊悉舉，諸道進攻，豈可俱絕其運糧，盡保其城壁？

translations.literal: Once the border regions all rise together and every circuit attacks, how can one cut off all their grain transport and fully defend every wall?
translations.idiomatic: Once every frontier district mobilizes and attacks from every direction, how can you cut off all their supplies and hold every fortress?

sentences.zh: 若諸險悉固，誠善莫加焉；

translations.literal: If every perilous pass were fully secured, nothing could be better;
translations.idiomatic: If every pass were impregnable, nothing could be better;

sentences.zh: 苟尺水橫流，則長堤虛設矣。

translations.literal: but if a foot of water flows across, the long embankment is set up in vain.
translations.idiomatic: but if water breaches even a foot of the line, the whole long dike is useless.

sentences.zh: 其次曰，或大朝用吳越之眾，自泉州泛海以趣國都，則不數日至城下矣。

translations.literal: Next they say that perhaps the Great Court will use the forces of Wu and Yue, sail from Quanzhou across the sea toward the capital, and in no more than a few days reach beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Others say the Great Court may use Wu-Yue troops, sail from Quanzhou across the sea to your capital, and reach your walls within days.

sentences.zh: 當其人心疑惑，兵勢動搖，岸上舟中皆為敵國，忠臣義士能復幾人？

translations.literal: When hearts are doubtful and military morale wavers, shore and ship alike become enemy country — how many loyal and righteous men can remain?
translations.idiomatic: When minds waver and armies falter, land and sea alike become enemy ground — how many loyal men will remain?

sentences.zh: 懷進退者步步生心，顧妻子者滔滔皆是。

translations.literal: Those weighing advance and retreat breed new schemes at every step; those looking to wife and children are a rushing flood.
translations.idiomatic: Men weighing flight will scheme at every step; men thinking of wives and children will be beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 變故難測，須臾萬端，非惟暫乖始圖，實恐有誤壯誌，又非巨舟之可及，滄海之可遊也。

translations.literal: Sudden changes are hard to foresee — in an instant ten thousand turns; not only might the first plan briefly fail, but one truly fears misleading a great ambition — and this is not something great ships can reach or the blue sea can be crossed for escape.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster is unpredictable; in a moment everything changes. You may not only miss your first plan but ruin your grand design — and this is no matter of great ships or escape upon the open sea.

sentences.zh: 然此等皆戰伐之常事，兵家之預謀，雖勝負未知，成敗相半。

translations.literal: Yet these are all ordinary affairs of warfare and forethought of strategists — though victory and defeat are unknown, success and failure are half and half.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all this is the common stuff of war and military planning — victory uncertain, success and failure each half likely.

sentences.zh: 苟不得已而為也，固斷在不疑；

translations.literal: If one must do it because there is no alternative, the decision is surely without doubt;
translations.idiomatic: If you must fight because there is no choice, the decision is clear;

sentences.zh: 若無大故而思之，又深可痛惜。

translations.literal: but if one contemplates it without great cause, it is deeply to be lamented.
translations.idiomatic: but to contemplate war without grave cause is deeply to be regretted.

sentences.zh: 且小之事大，理固然也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the small serving the great is reason's natural order.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the lesser serving the greater is the natural order of things.

sentences.zh: 遠古之例不能備談，本朝當楊氏之建吳也，亦入貢莊宗。

translations.literal: Ancient examples cannot all be discussed; in our dynasty, when the Yang clan founded Wu, they also paid tribute to Emperor Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient precedents are too many to recount, but when the Yang clan founded Wu in our own time, they too paid tribute to Emperor Zhuangzong.

sentences.zh: 恭自烈祖開基，中原多故，事大之禮，因循未遑，以至交兵，幾成危殆。

translations.literal: I respectfully reflect that since Liezu founded our state, the Central Plains have had many troubles and the rites of serving the great power were put off in delay, until arms were crossed and we nearly perished.
translations.idiomatic: Since our Founding Ancestor established the state, turmoil in the Central Plains delayed our observance of tribute to the suzerain until war broke out and we nearly perished.

sentences.zh: 非不欲憑大江之險，恃眾多之力，尋悟知難則退，遂修出境之盟；

translations.literal: It was not that we did not wish to rely on the Yangtze's peril and trust in numerous forces — we soon understood that when difficulty was known one should withdraw, and therefore restored the treaty beyond our borders;
translations.idiomatic: We did not lack the Yangtze's barrier or ample troops, but we saw that when the odds were impossible, retreat was wisdom, and we renewed the treaty beyond our borders;

sentences.zh: 一介之使才行，萬里之兵頓息，惠民和眾，於今賴之。

translations.literal: a single envoy had barely set out when armies ten thousand li away suddenly stilled — benefiting the people and harmonizing the masses, on which we still rely today.
translations.idiomatic: one envoy had barely departed when armies ten thousand li away stood down — the people were spared, the realm calmed, and we still live by that choice today.

sentences.zh: 自足下祖德之開基，亦通好中國，以闡霸圖。

translations.literal: Since Your Excellency's ancestral virtue opened the foundation, you too have maintained good relations with the Central Court to unfold a hegemonic design.
translations.idiomatic: Since your ancestors founded your realm, you too have kept peace with the Central Court while pursuing your own ambitions.

sentences.zh: 願修祖宗之謀，以尋中國之好，蕩無益之忿，棄不急之爭；

translations.literal: I wish you would renew your ancestors' policy, seek again the Central Court's goodwill, wash away useless wrath, and abandon unurgent contention;
translations.idiomatic: Renew your ancestors' policy, seek the Central Court's friendship again, cast off useless anger, and abandon a fight that cannot wait;

sentences.zh: 知存知亡，能強能弱，屈己以濟億兆，談笑而定國家，至德大業無虧也，宗廟社稷無損也。

translations.literal: know survival and ruin, be able to be strong or weak, bend yourself to aid the hundred millions, settle the state with a smile — supreme virtue and great enterprise without loss, ancestral temples and altars without harm.
translations.idiomatic: know when to survive and when to perish, be strong or yield as needed, humble yourself to save your people, settle the realm with ease — your supreme virtue and great enterprise intact, your temples and altars unharmed.

sentences.zh: 玉帛朝聘之禮才出於境，而天下之兵已息矣，豈不易如反掌，固如太山哉？

translations.literal: The rites of jade and silk, court audience and envoy mission, have barely left the border when the armies of the empire already cease — is it not easier than turning the hand, firmer than Mount Tai?
translations.idiomatic: Let tribute cross your border, and the empire's armies will stand down — easier than turning your hand, surer than Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 何必扼腕盱衡，履腸蹀血，然後為勇也。

translations.literal: Why must one clench the wrist and glare, tread the bowels and trample blood, and only then call it courage?
translations.idiomatic: Why must you clench your fists, glare about, tread guts and wade in blood before you call it courage?

sentences.zh: 故曰：「德如毛，民鮮克舉之，我儀圖之。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "Virtue is like a feather — the people can scarcely lift it; I will take it as my model.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "Virtue is light as a feather, yet few can bear it up; I will make it my aim.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「知止不殆，可以長久。

translations.literal: " It is also said: "Knowing when to stop brings no peril; one may endure long.
translations.idiomatic: " And: "Knowing when to stop avoids danger; thus one endures.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「沈潛剛克，高明柔克。

translations.literal: " It is also said: "The hidden and deep overcome by firmness; the lofty and bright overcome by softness.
translations.idiomatic: " And: "The hidden and firm overcome by steadfastness; the lofty and bright overcome by yielding.

sentences.zh: 」此聖賢之事業，何恥而不為哉？

translations.literal: " These are the enterprises of sages — what shame is there in not doing them?
translations.idiomatic: " These are the deeds of sages — what shame could there be in following them?

sentences.zh: 況大朝皇帝以命世之英，光宅中夏，承五運而乃當正統，度四方則咸偃下風；

translations.literal: Moreover, the Emperor of the Great Court is a hero of the age who illuminates the Central Xia, inherits the Five Movements and rightly holds the orthodox succession — surveying the four quarters, all bow beneath his wind;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Great Court's Emperor is a hero of the age who rules the Central Plains, holds the Mandate of the Five Phases, and commands the four quarters — all bow before him;

sentences.zh: 獫狁、太原固不勞於薄伐，南轅返旆更屬在於何人。

translations.literal: the Xianyun and Taiyuan certainly did not require a light campaign — who else could turn the southern chariot and return the banners?
translations.idiomatic: the Xiongnu and Taiyuan fell without a strenuous campaign — who else could turn south and bring the banners home?

sentences.zh: 又方且遏天下之兵鋒，俟貴國之嘉問，則大國之義斯亦以善矣，足下之忿亦可以息矣。

translations.literal: He is even now restraining the empire's military edge, awaiting your state's gracious inquiry — then the great state's righteousness will also be fulfilled, and Your Excellency's wrath can also be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: He is even now holding back the empire's armies, awaiting your gracious response — then the great state's honor will be satisfied and your anger can cease.

sentences.zh: 若介然不移，有利於宗廟社稷可也，有利於黎元可也，有利於天下可也，有利於身可也。

translations.literal: If you remain unmoved, it may benefit the ancestral temples and altars, benefit the black-haired people, benefit the empire, benefit yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If you stand firm, it must benefit your temples and altars, your people, the empire, or yourself.

sentences.zh: 凡是四者無一利焉，何用棄德修怨，自生仇敵，使赫赫南國，將成禍機，炎炎奈何，其可向邇？

translations.literal: Of these four there is not one that profits — why abandon virtue and cultivate enmity, create enemies yourself, and make the glorious Southern State about to become a seat of calamity — blazing heat, alas, how can one draw near?
translations.idiomatic: Yet none of the four will gain. Why abandon virtue and nurse hatred, make enemies of your own, and turn your glorious southern realm into a furnace of disaster — how can you draw near such flames?

sentences.zh: 幸而小勝也，莫保其後焉，不幸而違心，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: Even if by luck there is a small victory, nothing afterward can be secured; if unluckily it goes against the heart, then the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Even a small victory cannot secure what follows; if fortune turns against you, the great cause is lost.

sentences.zh: 復念頃者淮、泗交兵，疆陲多壘，吳越以累世之好，遂首為厲階；

translations.literal: I think again how recently on the Huai and Si arms were crossed and the borders had many ramparts — Wu and Yue, with goodwill of many generations, were the first to become the source of harm;
translations.idiomatic: I recall how recently war flared on the Huai and Si, how ramparts multiplied on the borders — Wu and Yue, despite generations of friendship, were first to break the peace;

sentences.zh: 惟有貴國情分逾親，歡盟愈篤，在先朝感義，情實慨然，下走承基，理難負德，不能自己，又馳此緘。

translations.literal: only your state has bonds more intimate, alliance more earnest — in the former reign moved by righteousness, the feeling was truly stirred; I who have inherited the foundation can hardly betray such virtue, cannot restrain myself, and again hurry this letter.
translations.idiomatic: only your state has been closer in bond and firmer in alliance. The former emperor was moved by your loyalty; I who inherited the throne cannot betray such debt. I cannot restrain myself and send this letter in haste.

sentences.zh: 近奉大朝諭旨，以為足下無通好之心，必舉上秋之役，即命弊邑速絕連盟。

translations.literal: Recently I received the Great Court's command, holding that Your Excellency has no heart for peace and will surely launch the late-autumn campaign, and immediately ordered my humble state swiftly to sever our linked alliance.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately received the Great Court's order, which holds that you have no wish for peace and will surely launch the late-autumn campaign, and commands my state at once to break our alliance.

sentences.zh: 雖善鄰之心，期於永保；

translations.literal: Though the heart of good neighborliness hopes for eternal preservation;
translations.idiomatic: Though my heart as a good neighbor hopes to preserve our bond forever;

sentences.zh: 而事大之節，焉敢固違。

translations.literal: the propriety of serving the great power — how dare I stubbornly disobey?
translations.idiomatic: the duty of serving the suzerain — how dare I defy it?

sentences.zh: 恐煜之不得事足下也，是以惻惻之意所不能雲，區區之誠於是乎在。

translations.literal: I fear that Yu may no longer be able to serve Your Excellency — therefore the anguished feeling that cannot be spoken, the humble sincerity that lies herein.
translations.idiomatic: I fear I may no longer be able to stand as your friend — hence the anguish I cannot fully express, and the humble sincerity of this letter.

sentences.zh: 又念臣子之情，尚不逾於三諫，煜之極言，於此三矣，是為臣者可以逃，為子者可以泣，為交友者亦惆悵而遂絕矣。

translations.literal: I think again that in the feeling of minister and son one does not go beyond three remonstrances — Yu's utmost words have now reached three; as minister one may withdraw, as son one may weep, as friend one may grieve and then break off.
translations.idiomatic: A loyal subject does not remonstrate more than thrice — I have spoken my utmost three times. As minister I may withdraw; as son I may weep; as friend I grieve and must part.

sentences.zh: 鋹得書，遂囚慎儀，驛書答煜，言甚不遜，煜上其書。

translations.literal: When Chang received the letter, he imprisoned Shenyi, replied to Yu by post with words very insubordinate, and Yu presented the letter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang received the letter, he imprisoned Shenyi, sent a courier's reply to Yu full of insolence, and Yu forwarded the letter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，太祖命潭州防禦使潘美、朗州團練使尹崇珂討之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao, Emperor Taizu ordered Tanzhou defense commissioner Pan Mei and Langzhou training commissioner Yin Chongke to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaibao (970), Emperor Taizu ordered Pan Mei, defense commissioner of Tanzhou, and Yin Chongke, training commissioner of Langzhou, to attack him.

sentences.zh: 八月，師至白霞，

translations.literal: In the eighth month the army reached Baixia,
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the army reached Baixia,

sentences.zh: 鋹賀州刺史陳守忠告急於鋹。

translations.literal: and He prefecture prefect Chen Shouzhong reported the emergency to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: and He Prefect Chen Shouzhong reported the emergency to Chang.

sentences.zh: 時舊將多以讒構誅死，宗室翦滅殆盡，掌兵者唯宦人數輩。

translations.literal: At the time many old generals had been executed on framed slander, the imperial clan was nearly exterminated, and those who held military authority were only a few eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: By then most veteran generals had been executed on framed charges, the imperial clan was nearly wiped out, and only a handful of eunuchs held military command.

sentences.zh: 自晟以來，耽於遊宴，城壁壕隍多飾為宮館池沼，樓艦皆毀，兵器又腐，內外震恐。

translations.literal: Since Sheng's time [the court] had been addicted to feasting and pleasure; city walls and moats were largely ornamented into palaces, lodges, and ponds; tower ships were all destroyed and weapons rotted — within and without, all trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Since Sheng's reign the court had indulged in feasts and games; walls and moats were turned into palaces and ponds, warships dismantled, weapons left to rot — the realm was shaken with fear inside and out.

sentences.zh: 乃遣龔澄樞往賀州，郭崇嶽往桂州，李托往韶州，畫守禦之策。

translations.literal: He then sent Gong Chengshu to He prefecture, Guo Chongyue to Gui prefecture, and Li Tuo to Shao prefecture to draft plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Gong Chengshu to He, Guo Chongyue to Gui, and Li Tuo to Shao to plan the defense.

sentences.zh: 九月，美與崇珂圍賀州，澄樞遁歸。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Mei and Chongke besieged He prefecture; Chengshu fled back.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Pan Mei and Yin Chongke besieged He Prefecture, and Gong Chengshu fled home.

sentences.zh: 鋹遣大將伍彥柔領兵赴賀，美等以奇兵伏南鄉岸。

translations.literal: Chang sent the great general Wu Yanrou to lead troops to relieve He; Mei and others set an ambush with elite troops on the south-bank shore.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent his general Wu Yanrou with troops to relieve He, while Mei laid an ambush with picked men on the southern shore.

sentences.zh: 彥柔夜至，艤舟岸側，遲明挾彈登岸，踞胡床指麾。

translations.literal: Yanrou arrived at night, moored his boats by the shore, and at dawn came ashore with a pellet-bow, seated on a folding camp chair to command.
translations.idiomatic: Yanrou arrived at night and moored along the bank. At dawn he came ashore with a pellet-bow and sat on a camp chair to direct his men.

sentences.zh: 伏兵卒發，彥柔眾大亂，死者千人。

translations.literal: The ambush suddenly sprang; Yanrou's force fell into great disorder and a thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush struck; Yanrou's army collapsed, and a thousand men were killed.

sentences.zh: 擒彥柔斬之，梟首以示城中。

translations.literal: They captured Yanrou and beheaded him, displaying the head to show the city.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Yanrou, beheaded him, and displayed his head before the city.

sentences.zh: 翌日，城陷。

translations.literal: The next day the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the city fell.

sentences.zh: 美等督戰艦，聲言順流趨廣州，鋹令都統潘崇徹將兵五萬屯賀江。

translations.literal: Mei and others directed the war fleet, declaring they would go downstream toward Guangzhou; Chang ordered commander-in-chief Pan Chongche to lead fifty thousand troops to camp on the He River.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mei led the fleet downstream toward Guangzhou in name, while Chang ordered Commander-in-Chief Pan Chongche to camp fifty thousand men on the He River.

sentences.zh: 十月，美等次昭州，破開建砦，殺卒數百，擒砦將靳暉，昭州刺史田行稠遁去，城遂陷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Mei and others halted at Shao prefecture, broke the Kaijian stockade, killed several hundred soldiers, captured stockade commander Jin Hui; Shao prefect Tian Xingchou fled, and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they reached Shao Prefecture, stormed the Kaijian stockade, killed hundreds, and captured its commander Jin Hui. Prefect Tian Xingchou fled, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 桂州刺史李承進棄城亦奔。

translations.literal: Gui prefect Li Chengjin also abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Prefect Li Chengjin abandoned his city and fled as well.

sentences.zh: 十一月，連州陷，招討使盧收率眾退保清遠。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Lian prefecture fell; pacification commissioner Lu Shou led his forces back to hold Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Lian Prefecture fell, and Pacification Commissioner Lu Shou withdrew to defend Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，美等攻韶州，都統李承渥以兵數萬陣蓮華山下。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Mei and others attacked Shao prefecture; commander-in-chief Li Chenwo arrayed tens of thousands of troops below Lotus Flower Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they attacked Shao Prefecture, where Commander-in-Chief Li Chenwo drew up tens of thousands of men below Lotus Flower Mountain.

sentences.zh: 初，鋹教象為陣，每象載十數人，皆執兵仗，凡戰必置陣前，以壯軍威。

translations.literal: Earlier Chang had trained elephants for battle; each elephant carried a dozen or so men, all holding weapons, and in every fight they were placed before the line to bolster military awe.
translations.idiomatic: Chang had trained war elephants, each carrying a dozen armed men placed before the battle line to terrify the enemy.

sentences.zh: 至是與美遇，美盡索軍中勁弩布前以射之，象奔踶，乘象者皆墜，反踐承渥軍，遂大敗，承渥僅以身免。

translations.literal: When they now met Mei, Mei gathered all the army's powerful crossbows and arrayed them forward to shoot; the elephants stampeded and kicked, those riding them all fell, and they turned back to trample Chenwo's army — a great defeat, Chenwo barely escaping with his life.
translations.idiomatic: When they met Pan Mei, he lined up his strongest crossbows and shot the elephants. The beasts stampeded, riders fell, and the elephants trampled Li Chenwo's army. Li Chenwo barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 韶州陷，擒刺史辛延渥、諫議大夫卿文遠。

translations.literal: Shao prefecture fell; they captured prefect Xin Yanwo and remonstrance grandee Qing Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Prefecture fell. They captured Prefect Xin Yanwo and Remonstrance Grandee Qing Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 鋹始令塹廣州東壕，遣郭崇嶽統兵六萬屯馬逕，列柵以拒之。

translations.literal: Chang then ordered trenches dug along Guangzhou's eastern moat and sent Guo Chongyue to command sixty thousand troops camped at Majing, setting palisades to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Chang ordered trenches dug along Guangzhou's eastern moat and sent Guo Chongyue with sixty thousand men to camp at Majing and build palisades to block the advance.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，美等破英、雄二州，都統潘崇徹來降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year Mei and others took Ying and Xiong prefectures; commander-in-chief Pan Chongche came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year (971) they captured Ying and Xiong prefectures, and Commander-in-Chief Pan Chongche surrendered.

sentences.zh: 翌日，次瀧頭，鋹遣使請和，且求緩師。

translations.literal: The next day they halted at Longtou; Chang sent envoys to sue for peace and also asked that the army be slowed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they halted at Longtou. Chang sent envoys to sue for peace and beg for a delay.

sentences.zh: 瀧頭山水險惡，美等疑有伏兵，乃挾鋹使速度諸險。

translations.literal: Longtou's mountains and waters were perilous and harsh; Mei and others suspected an ambush and therefore took Chang's envoy along to hurry through the dangers.
translations.idiomatic: Longtou's terrain was treacherous. Suspecting an ambush, Mei took Chang's envoy along to hurry through the passes.

sentences.zh: 二月，過馬逕，去廣城十里，砦於雙女山下。

translations.literal: In the second month they passed Majing, ten li from Guang city, and encamped below Twin Maidens Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month they passed Majing, ten li from Guangzhou, and encamped below Twin Maidens Mountain.

sentences.zh: 鋹聞之，取舶船十餘艘，載金寶、妃嬪欲入海。

translations.literal: When Chang heard this, he took more than ten ocean-going ships, loaded gold, treasures, and consorts, intending to flee to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Chang prepared more than ten seagoing ships loaded with gold, treasures, and consorts, intending to flee across the sea.

sentences.zh: 未及發，宦官樂範與衛兵千餘盜舶船走。

translations.literal: Before he could depart, the eunuch Yue Fan and more than a thousand guards stole the ships and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could sail, the eunuch Yue Fan and more than a thousand guards stole the ships and fled.

sentences.zh: 美等將至城，鋹懼，遣其右僕射蕭漼奉表詣軍門乞降。

translations.literal: As Mei and others were about to reach the city, Chang in fear sent his right vice director Xiao Huan with a memorial to the army gate to beg surrender.
translations.idiomatic: As the army neared the city, Chang in terror sent his Right Vice Director Xiao Huan with a memorial to the camp gate to surrender.

sentences.zh: 美諭太祖意，語在《美傳》。

translations.literal: Mei conveyed Taizu's intent — the words are in the Biography of Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mei conveyed Taizu's intent, as recorded in his biography.

sentences.zh: 使者乞部送赴闕，師遂頓城外。

translations.literal: The envoy asked to be escorted to the court; the army then halted outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy asked to be escorted to court, and the army halted outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 鋹又遣其弟保興率百官奉迎，為郭崇嶽所遏。

translations.literal: Chang again sent his younger brother Baoxing leading the hundred officials to welcome them, but was blocked by Guo Chongyue.
translations.idiomatic: Chang then sent his brother Baoxing with the officials to welcome the army, but Guo Chongyue blocked them.

sentences.zh: 崇嶽無謀勇，但祈禱鬼神，復為拒捍之備。

translations.literal: Chongyue lacked strategy and courage and only prayed to spirits and ghosts, again making preparations to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyue had neither strategy nor courage; he prayed to gods and ghosts and prepared to resist again.

sentences.zh: 美等乃進攻，保興迎戰，大為所敗，美乘風縱火，煙埃坌起，崇嶽死於亂兵。

translations.literal: Mei and others then pressed the attack; Baoxing met them in battle and was greatly defeated; Mei rode the wind to set fires, dust and smoke billowing up, and Chongyue died among the disorderly troops.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mei attacked. Baoxing met him and was routed. Mei set fires on the wind; dust and smoke rose in clouds, and Guo Chongyue died in the rout.

sentences.zh: 城既破，鋹盡焚其府庫。

translations.literal: When the city was broken, Chang burned all his treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Chang burned his treasuries.

sentences.zh: 美擒鋹及龔澄樞、李托、薛崇譽與宗室文武九十七人，同縻於龍德宮。

translations.literal: Mei captured Chang together with Gong Chengshu, Li Tuo, Xue Chongyu, and ninety-seven members of the imperial clan and civil and military officials, all confined together in Longde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mei captured Chang along with Gong Chengshu, Li Tuo, Xue Chongyu, and ninety-seven imperial clansmen and officials, and confined them in Longde Palace.

sentences.zh: 保興逃於民家，亦獲之，悉部送闕下。

translations.literal: Baoxing fled into a commoner's house but was also taken; all were escorted to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing hid in a commoner's house but was captured too. All were escorted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 斬閹工五百餘人。

translations.literal: More than five hundred castrated artisans were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred eunuch craftsmen were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 凡得州六十、縣二百十四、戶十七萬。

translations.literal: In all they gained sixty prefectures, two hundred fourteen counties, and one hundred seventy thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In all they gained sixty prefectures, two hundred fourteen counties, and one hundred seventy thousand households.

sentences.zh: 鋹至江陵，邸吏龐師進迎謁，學士黃德昭侍鋹，鋹問師進何人，德昭曰：「本國人也。

translations.literal: When Chang reached Jiangling, lodge clerk Pang Shijin came to welcome and pay respects; academician Huang Dezhao attended Chang; Chang asked who Shijin was, and Dezhao said, "He is a man of our state.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling, lodge clerk Pang Shijin came to greet him. Academician Huang Dezhao attended Chang, who asked who Shijin was. Dezhao said, "He is one of our countrymen.

sentences.zh: 」鋹曰：「何為在此？

translations.literal: " Chang said, "Why is he here?
translations.idiomatic: " Chang asked, "Why is he here?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「先主歲貢大朝，輜重比至荊州，乃令師進至邸，於此造車，以給饋運爾。

translations.literal: " He said, "The former ruler yearly paid tribute to the Great Court; when baggage trains reached Jingzhou, he ordered Shijin to the lodge to build carts here to supply the transport of provisions."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Our former ruler sent annual tribute to the Great Court. When the baggage trains reached Jingzhou, he stationed Shijin at the lodge to build carts here for the supply convoys."

sentences.zh: 」鋹歎曰：「我在位十四年，未嘗聞此言，今日始知祖宗山河及大朝境土也。

translations.literal: " Chang sighed and said, "I was on the throne fourteen years and never heard this said — today I first know our ancestors' mountains and rivers and the Great Court's territory."
translations.idiomatic: " Chang sighed, "I ruled fourteen years and never heard this. Today I first learn what our ancestors' realm and the Great Court's lands truly were."

sentences.zh: 」因泣涕久之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon wept for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: " He wept for a long time.

sentences.zh: 至京，舍於玉津園，太祖遣參知政事呂餘慶問鋹翻覆及焚府庫之罪，鋹歸罪澄樞、托、崇譽。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital he was lodged in Jade Ford Garden; Taizu sent participation councillor Lü Yuqing to question Chang about his reversals and the crime of burning the treasuries; Chang laid the blame on Chengshu, Tuo, and Chongyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he was lodged at Jade Ford Garden. Taizu sent Vice Councilor Lü Yuqing to question him about his rebellions and burning the treasuries. Chang blamed Chengshu, Tuo, and Chongyu.

sentences.zh: 翌日，有司以帛係鋹及其官屬獻太廟、太社。

translations.literal: The next day the authorities bound Chang and his officials with silk cords and presented them at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Altar of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: The next day officials bound Chang and his retinue with silk cords and presented them at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Altar of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 太祖禦明德門，遣攝刑部尚書盧多遜宣詔責鋹，鋹對曰：「臣年十六僭偽位，澄樞等皆先臣舊人，每事臣不得專，在國時臣是臣下，澄樞是國主。

translations.literal: Taizu took the throne at Bright Virtue Gate and sent acting Minister of Justice Lu Duoxun to proclaim the edict rebuking Chang; Chang replied, "Your subject at sixteen presumptuously took the false throne; Chengshu and the others were all my father's old men — in every matter your subject could not decide alone. In the state your subject was the subject, and Chengshu was the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu appeared at Bright Virtue Gate and sent Acting Minister of Justice Lu Duoxun to read the edict of rebuke. Chang answered, "I usurped the throne at sixteen. Chengshu and the others were my father's old retainers; I could decide nothing alone. In our state I was the subject and Chengshu was the ruler.

sentences.zh: 」遂伏地待罪。

translations.literal: " He then prostrated himself to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " He prostrated himself to await judgment.

sentences.zh: 太祖命攝大理卿高繼申引澄樞、托、崇譽斬於千秋門外。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered acting chief justice of the Court of Judicial Review Gao Jishen to lead Chengshu, Tuo, and Chongyu out and behead them outside Thousand Autumns Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu ordered Acting Chief Justice Gao Jishen to execute Chengshu, Tuo, and Chongyu outside Thousand Autumns Gate.

sentences.zh: 釋鋹罪，賜襲衣、冠帶、器幣、鞍勒馬，授金紫光祿大夫、檢校太保、右千牛衛大將軍、員外置同正員，封恩赦侯，朝會班上將軍之下。

translations.literal: Chang's crime was pardoned; he was granted court robes, cap and belt, vessels and silks, saddle and bridle and horse; appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Purple Tally, acting Grand Guardian, General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard with supernumerary status equal to regular, enfeoffed as Marquis of Enpardon; at court assemblies he stood below full generals.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was pardoned and given court robes, cap and belt, gifts, saddle, and horse. He was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Purple Tally, Acting Grand Guardian, and General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard with supernumerary rank, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Enpardon, taking his place at court below full generals.

sentences.zh: 以其弟保興為右監門率府率，左僕射蕭漼為太子中允，中書舍人卓惟休為太僕寺丞，餘並署諸州上佐、縣令、主簿。

translations.literal: His younger brother Baoxing was made captain of the Right Palace Gate Guard; left vice director Xiao Huan was made palace companion to the heir apparent; Secretariat drafter Zhuo Weixiu was made vice director of the Imperial Stud; the rest were all assigned as senior aides in prefectures, magistrates, and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Baoxing became captain of the Right Palace Gate Guard; Left Vice Director Xiao Huan became palace companion to the heir apparent; Secretariat Drafter Zhuo Weixiu became vice director of the Imperial Stud; the rest received posts as prefectural aides, magistrates, and clerks.

sentences.zh: 初，時嘗召司天監周傑筮之，遇《復》之《豐》，問曰：「享年幾何？

translations.literal: Earlier, in [the earlier ruler's] time, the Director of the Astronomy Bureau Zhou Jie was summoned to divine by milfoil; he obtained Return changing to Abundance, and [the ruler] asked, "How many years of life?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Director of the Astronomy Bureau Zhou Jie had been summoned to cast the milfoil. The hexagram was Return changing to Abundance. The ruler asked, "How many years will the dynasty endure?

sentences.zh: 」傑曰：「凡二卦皆土為應，土之數五，二五，十也，上下各五，將五百五十五乎。

translations.literal: " Jie said, "In both hexagrams earth is the corresponding line; earth's number is five — two fives make ten; upper and lower each five — perhaps five hundred fifty-five?"
translations.idiomatic: " Jie said, "In both hexagrams the corresponding line is earth. Earth's number is five; two fives make ten; upper and lower each have five — perhaps five hundred fifty-five years?"

sentences.zh: 」及鋹之敗，果五十五年，蓋傑舉成數以避一時之害爾。

translations.literal: " When Chang was defeated, it was indeed fifty-five years — presumably Jie cited a round number to avoid immediate harm.
translations.idiomatic: " When Chang fell, it had indeed been fifty-five years — Jie had cited a round number to avoid immediate punishment.

sentences.zh: 又廣州童謠曰：「羊頭二四，白天雨至。

translations.literal: There was also a children's rhyme in Guangzhou: "Sheep's head two-four, white sky rain comes.
translations.idiomatic: A children's rhyme in Guangzhou ran: "Sheep's head, two and four; white sky, rain will pour.

sentences.zh: 」識者以羊是未之神，是歲歲在辛未，以二月四日擒鋹。

translations.literal: " Those who understood took sheep as the spirit of wei (the eighth branch); that year was xinwei, and on the second month's fourth day Chang was captured.
translations.idiomatic: " Interpreters took sheep as the sign wei; that year was xinwei (the year of the sheep), and Chang was captured on the fourth day of the second month.

sentences.zh: 天雨者，王師如時雨之義。

translations.literal: Heaven's rain meant the royal army in the sense of timely rain.
translations.idiomatic: "Rain from heaven" meant the imperial army arriving like timely rain.

sentences.zh: 又前一年九月八日夕，眾星皆北流，有知星者言，劉氏歸朝之兆也。

translations.literal: Also on the evening of the eighth day of the ninth month the year before, all the stars flowed northward; one who knew the stars said it was an omen of the Liu clan returning to the court.
translations.idiomatic: On the evening of the eighth day of the ninth month the year before, all the stars seemed to drift northward. An astronomer said this foretold the Liu clan's submission to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔鋹月給增錢五萬、米麥五十斛。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict increased Chang's monthly stipend by fifty thousand cash and fifty bushels of rice and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year an edict raised his monthly stipend by fifty thousand cash and fifty bushels of grain.

sentences.zh: 八年，李煜平，遷左監門衛上將軍，進封彭城郡公。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when Li Yu was pacified, [Chang] was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Palace Gate Guard and advanced to Duke of Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after Li Yu's surrender, he was made General-in-Chief of the Left Palace Gate Guard and advanced to Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，又進衛國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was further advanced to Duke of Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he was further advanced to Duke of Weiguo.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died at the age of thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，贈太師，追封南越王。

translations.literal: Court was suspended three days; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and retroactively enfeoffed as King of Southern Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning lasted three days. He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as King of Southern Yue.

sentences.zh: 鋹體質豐碩，眉目俱竦。

translations.literal: Chang's physique was full and large, his brows and eyes both prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was stout of build, with prominent brows and eyes.

sentences.zh: 有口辯，性絕巧，嘗以珠結鞍勒為戲龍之狀，極其精妙，以獻太祖。

translations.literal: He had eloquence in speech and a nature of surpassing skill; he once used pearls to knot saddle and bridle into the form of a playful dragon, extremely refined in its finesse, and presented it to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: He was eloquent and possessed extraordinary skill. Once he wove pearls into saddle and bridle in the shape of a playful dragon, executed with exquisite finesse, and presented it to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔示諸宮官，皆駭伏，遂以錢百五十萬給其直，謂左右臣曰：「鋹好工巧，習以成性，儻能以習巧之勤移於治國，豈至滅亡哉！」

translations.literal: Taizu had it shown to the palace officials, all of whom were awestruck and prostrated; he then gave one million five hundred thousand cash for its price and said to the ministers at his side, "Chang loves craftsmanship — it has become his nature through habit; if he could shift the diligence of practicing skill to governing the state, how would he have come to ruin!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu displayed it to the palace officials, who were all awestruck. He paid one million five hundred thousand cash for it and told his ministers, "Chang loves craftsmanship — it has become second nature. Had he applied that diligence to governing his realm, how would he have fallen?"

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗乘肩輿從十數騎幸講武池，從官未集，鋹先至，賜鋹卮酒。

translations.literal: Taizu once rode a shoulder carriage with a dozen or so horsemen to visit the Martial Instruction Pool; the attending officials were not yet assembled when Chang arrived first, and [Taizu] granted Chang a goblet of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once rode in a shoulder carriage with a dozen horsemen to the Martial Instruction Pool. Before his attendants had gathered, Chang arrived first, and Taizu offered him a cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 鋹疑為冘，泣曰：「臣承祖父基業，違拒韓廷，勞王師致討，罪固當死，陛下不殺臣，今見太平，為大梁布衣足矣。

translations.literal: Chang suspected it was poisoned wine and wept, saying, "Your subject inherited my grandfather's foundation, defied and resisted the Han court, and troubled the royal army to campaign against me — the crime surely deserved death. Your Majesty did not kill your subject; now I see peace — to be a common cloth-clad man of Great Liang is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Chang feared it was poisoned wine and wept, saying, "I inherited my grandfather's realm, defied the Song court, and brought the imperial army down upon me — I deserved death. Your Majesty spared me; now I see peace, and to live as a commoner of Great Song is blessing enough.

sentences.zh: 願延旦夕之命，以全陛下生成之恩，臣未敢飲此酒。

translations.literal: I wish to prolong my life day by day, to fulfill Your Majesty's grace in giving life — your subject dares not drink this wine.
translations.idiomatic: I beg only to live out my days and repay your grace in sparing my life. I dare not drink this cup.

sentences.zh: 」太祖笑曰：「朕推心於人腹，安有此事！

translations.literal: " Taizu laughed and said, "I open my heart to men's innermost parts — how could there be such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu laughed. "I give men my full trust — how could I do such a thing?

sentences.zh: 」命取鋹酒自飲之，別酌以賜，鋹大慚頓首謝。

translations.literal: " He ordered Chang's wine taken and drunk himself, poured another cup to grant him, and Chang in great shame bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Chang's cup brought and drank from it himself, then poured another for Chang. Chang bowed deeply in shame and gratitude.

sentences.zh: 太宗將討晉陽，召近臣宴，鋹預之，自言：「朝廷威靈及遠，四方僭竊之主，今日盡在坐中，旦夕平太原，劉繼元又至，臣率先來朝，願得執梃為諸國降王長。

translations.literal: When Taizong was about to campaign against Jinyang, he summoned the near ministers to a feast; Chang was among them and said of himself, "The court's majesty and spirit reach far — the presumptuous usurpers of the four quarters are all seated here today. Within days Taiyuan will be pacified and Liu Jiyuan will also arrive; your subject came first to court and wishes to hold the staff as chief among the surrendered kings of the states.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong prepared to attack Jinyang, he feasted his close ministers. Chang was present and said, "The court's majesty reaches far. Every rebel ruler in the land sits at this table today. Taiyuan will fall within days, and Liu Jiyuan will join us. I came to court first and wish to lead the procession of surrendered kings with staff in hand.

sentences.zh: 」太宗大笑，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: " Taizong laughed greatly and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong laughed heartily and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 其詼諧此類也。

translations.literal: His wit and humor were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His humor was of this kind.

sentences.zh: 鋹子守節、守正，皆至崇儀副使。

translations.literal: Chang's sons Shoujie and Shouzheng both reached the post of vice commissioner of Honored Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's sons Shoujie and Shouzheng both rose to vice commissioner of Honored Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 守正卒，帝聞其家貧，詔月給萬錢。

translations.literal: When Shouzheng died, the Emperor heard his family was poor and ordered ten thousand cash given monthly.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouzheng died, the Emperor learned his family was poor and ordered ten thousand cash paid to them each month.

sentences.zh: 守素，咸平中為侍禁，亦貧，真宗賜白金百兩，語宰相曰：「諸偽主子孫率多窘迫，蓋僭侈之後不知稼穡艱難所致也。

translations.literal: Shousu, in the Xianping era was a palace guard attendant and also poor; Zhenzong granted a hundred taels of white gold and said to the chief ministers, "The descendants of the false rulers are mostly in straits — likely because after presumptuous extravagance they do not know the hardship of sowing and reaping.
translations.idiomatic: Shousu served as a palace guard attendant during Xianping and was also poor. Zhenzong gave him a hundred taels of silver and told the chief ministers, "The descendants of former rebel rulers are mostly destitute — the legacy of extravagant usurpation, never having learned the hardship of the fields.

sentences.zh: 」後至內殿崇班，天禧中，又錄為閣門祗候。

translations.literal: " Later he reached Inner Hall Honored Company; in the Tianxi era he was again enrolled as usher of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: " He later rose to Inner Hall Honored Company, and in the Tianxi era was appointed usher of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 守通，供奉官。

translations.literal: Shoutong was a tribute attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shoutong served as a tribute attendant.

sentences.zh: 守正子克昌，為三班奉職；

translations.literal: Shouzheng's son Kechang was a third-rank service officer;
translations.idiomatic: Shouzheng's son Kechang held a third-rank service post;

sentences.zh: 國昌，為借職。

translations.literal: Guochang held a borrowed-rank post.
translations.idiomatic: Guochang held a borrowed-rank post.

sentences.zh: 龔澄樞，廣州南海人。

translations.literal: Gong Chengshu was a man of Nanhai in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Chengshu was from Nanhai in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 性廉謹，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: His nature was frugal and cautious; he did not associate casually.
translations.idiomatic: He was frugal and cautious and did not socialize casually.

sentences.zh: 幼事為內供奉官，累遷內給事。

translations.literal: In youth he served [the earlier ruler] as inner tribute attendant and was repeatedly promoted to inner provisioner.
